project.name: Web3Connect
project.description: Interactive learning hub showing how Frontend, Backend, Database, and Blockchain work together from root to deployment.

sections.title: What is it?
sections.content: The frontend is the client-side React SPA users interact with. Built with React 19 and Vite 7, it provides modern UI with wallet integration via wagmi.

sections.title: Why is it used?
sections.content: SPA architecture gives instant navigation, rich UX, and seamless wallet connections. React's component model and ecosystem make complex UIs manageable.

sections.title: Tech Stack
sections.content: React 19 · Vite 7.3 · Tailwind CSS 3.4 · React Router 7.8 · Axios 1.7 · TanStack Query 5 · Framer Motion 12 · wagmi 3.6 · viem 2.48 · Socket.IO Client 4.8

flow.text: wagmi calls MetaMask to sign SIWE message
React updates auth context → redirects to dashboard

sections.title: Code: wagmi + Axios

qa.q: How does React communicate with Express?
qa.a: Through Axios HTTP client. Axios sends REST API calls (GET/POST/PUT/DELETE) to the Express backend running on port 5001. The backend returns JSON responses which React uses to update UI.

qa.q: How does the frontend connect to blockchain?
qa.a: Using wagmi library (built on viem/ethers.js). wagmi manages wallet connections (MetaMask), signs transactions, and reads contract data. The frontend never holds private keys.

qa.q: What happens when a user signs in?
qa.a: 1) Frontend requests a nonce from backend 2) User signs the nonce with MetaMask 3) Backend verifies the signature using ethers.verifyMessage() 4) JWT token issued 5) Frontend stores token and redirects.

qa.q: How is Socket.IO used in the frontend?
qa.a: The Socket.IO client connects to the same Express server. It emits events (send-message, typing) and listens for events (new-message, user-typing). This enables real-time chat without polling.

sections.title: What is it?
sections.content: Express server handling business logic, auth, file uploads, and blockchain interactions. Serves REST APIs with 16 route files (50+ endpoints).

flow.text: Middleware: CORS → Logger → Rate Limiter → Auth
Controller calls Mongoose model (DB) or ethers (Blockchain)
JSON response sent back to frontend

sections.title: Code: Route + Controller

qa.q: How does backend connect to MongoDB?
qa.a: Via Mongoose ODM. The connectDB() function calls mongoose.connect(MONGO_URI) with DNS retry logic. Mongoose provides schema validation, population (JOINs), and middleware hooks.

qa.q: How does backend connect to blockchain?
qa.a: Using ethers.js library. The backend creates an ethers.Wallet from the server's private key, connects to Polygon RPC, and calls the CertificateNFT contract to mint NFTs.
CORS (cross-origin), Helmet (security headers), Morgan (request logging), express-rate-limit (100 req/min), express-validator (input validation), and custom JWT auth middleware.

sections.title: What is it?
sections.content: MongoDB Atlas (cloud NoSQL database) with 19 Mongoose schemas. Stores users, communities, tasks, certificates, messages, and blockchain job queues.

flow.text: users — User profiles with wallet addresses, roles, verification status
communities — Groups with members, tasks, collaboration rooms
tasks — Assignments with submissions, due dates, NFT rewards
certificates — NFT metadata with IPFS URIs, tx hashes, token IDs
messages — DMs, group chats, server channels, voice messages

sections.title: Code: Mongoose Model

qa.q: How does Mongoose connect Express to MongoDB?
qa.a: Mongoose acts as an ODM (Object Document Mapper). Express controllers call Model.find() which Mongoose translates to MongoDB queries. Results return as JavaScript objects.

qa.q: What are Mongoose references vs embedded docs?
qa.a: Refs (ObjectId) store references to other documents — Mongoose .populate() resolves them (like SQL JOINs). Embedded docs store sub-documents directly within parent docs.

sections.title: What is it?
sections.content: Polygon Amoy testnet (chain ID 80002) with a Solidity smart contract (CertificateNFT) that mints ERC-721 soulbound tokens.

flow.text: Image uploaded to IPFS via Pinata
Transaction mined on Polygon Amoy → NFT exists on-chain

sections.title: Code: Smart Contract

qa.q: How does the backend talk to the blockchain?
qa.a: The backend has an ethers.Wallet with the server's private key. It creates a Contract instance using the deployed contract's ABI and address. Calling contract.mintCertificate() submits a transaction signed by the server wallet.

qa.q: What is the difference between blockchain and database?
qa.a: Database: centralized, mutable, fast CRUD. Blockchain: decentralized, immutable, trustless. Web3Connect uses BOTH — MongoDB for app data, blockchain for certificate authenticity.

qa.q: What is Polygon Amoy and why use a testnet?
qa.a: Polygon Amoy is a test network (testnet) for Polygon where MATIC tokens are free. It's used for development before deploying to mainnet (real money). Chain ID: 80002.

sections.title: What is it?
sections.content: Soulbound NFT certificates minted when students complete community tasks. Each is an ERC-721 token with metadata on IPFS and a visual certificate image.

flow.text: Upload image to IPFS via Pinata API
Create ERC-721 metadata JSON with image URI
Save record (txHash, tokenId, URIs) in MongoDB

sections.title: Code: Minting Service

qa.q: How does the NFT get from the contract to the user's wallet?
qa.a: The contract.mintCertificate() function calls _safeMint(student, tokenId), which creates the token and assigns ownership to the student's wallet address. The student sees it in MetaMask.
The contract overrides transferFrom(), safeTransferFrom(), and approve() to always revert. This means the NFT can never be transferred — it stays with the original owner forever.

sections.title: What is it?
sections.content: IPFS (InterPlanetary File System) is a decentralized P2P file protocol. Files are addressed by content hash (CID). Pinata is a pinning service that ensures files stay available.

sections.title: Why both IPFS and MongoDB?
sections.content: MongoDB stores app data (what can change). IPFS stores certificate images and metadata (must be immutable). The NFT's tokenURI points to IPFS — if the content changes, the CID hash changes, proving tampering.

sections.title: Code: Pinata Upload

qa.a: MongoDB holds dynamic app data (profiles, messages). IPFS holds immutable certificate assets — if someone alters the image, the CID changes, proving authenticity. The blockchain stores the IPFS hash.

sections.title: What is it?
sections.content: Two auth methods: JWT (email/password) and SIWE (Sign-In with Ethereum wallet). JWT tokens expire in 7 days and carry user role in payload.

flow.text: User signs the nonce with MetaMask private key
Recovered address must match walletAddress in request
JWT generated and returned → frontend stores it

sections.title: Code: Auth Middleware

qa.q: How does SIWE work step by step?
qa.a: 1) Server generates a one-time nonce (random hex) 2) Client asks MetaMask to sign it 3) Server recovers the signer's address via ethers.verifyMessage() 4) If it matches the claimed wallet → authenticated.

flow.text: Auth — register, login, wallet-login, SIWE, profile
Tasks — create, submit, grade, complete, issue certificates
Blockchain — mint NFT, check status, diagnose, retry

qa.q: How do routes connect frontend to database?
qa.a: Frontend calls Axios GET /api/communities → Express matches to router → Controller queries Community.find() → Mongoose returns documents → JSON response sent back.

sections.title: What is it?
sections.content: Socket.IO enables bidirectional real-time communication. Features: DMs, typing indicators, read receipts, server channels, voice messages, WebRTC calls, collaboration canvas.

sections.title: Code: Socket.IO Server

qa.q: How is Socket.IO different from HTTP?
qa.a: HTTP is request-response (client asks, server answers). Socket.IO maintains a persistent connection where either side can push data anytime — essential for chat, notifications, live cursors.

flow.text: Frontend → GitHub Pages (static build: npm run build)

qa.q: How do all pieces communicate in production?
qa.a: Frontend (GitHub Pages) makes API calls to Backend (Render) via HTTPS. Backend connects to MongoDB Atlas and Polygon Amoy. Wallet interactions (MetaMask) happen client-side connecting directly to Polygon.

flowSteps.title: 1. Student Joins Community
flowSteps.desc: Student finds a community via the dashboard, clicks Join. Frontend sends POST /api/communities/:id/join with the JWT token.

flowSteps.title: 2. Admin Creates Tasks
flowSteps.desc: Community admin creates tasks with deadlines. Tasks stored in MongoDB with references to community ID. Students can view tasks in the community page.

flowSteps.title: 3. Student Submits Work
flowSteps.desc: Student uploads files, adds notes, marks task as complete. Backend validates submission, stores files via Multer, updates task status in MongoDB.

flowSteps.title: 4. Certificate Image Generated
flowSteps.desc: Backend generates a 3200x2200px certificate using node-canvas. Certificate includes student name, community name, date, and unique serial number.

flowSteps.title: 5. Upload to IPFS via Pinata
flowSteps.desc: Certificate image sent to Pinata API. Returns an IPFS CID. Then metadata JSON (name, description, image URI) is also uploaded to IPFS.

flowSteps.title: 6. NFT Minted on Polygon
flowSteps.desc: Backend calls CertificateNFT.mintCertificate() on Polygon Amoy. The smart contract assigns token ownership to the student's wallet address.

flowSteps.title: 7. Record Saved in MongoDB
flowSteps.desc: Transaction hash, token ID, IPFS URIs saved to MongoDB. Student can view their NFT certificate in the dashboard → Certificates tab.

flowSteps.title: 8. Anyone Can Verify On-Chain
flowSteps.desc: Certificate page shows a 'Verify on Explorer' link → opens Polygonscan showing the mint transaction. The NFT is permanently linked to the student's wallet.
